title: Eating near the theaters and the Braddock Bar
summary: Cooks like Mom Baker fed musicians for 50 cents, performers gathered at the Braddock Bar, and the four-city circuit was called around the world.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You know, most theaters we played, somewhere on that block or on that street there would be some lady who cooked Mom Baker was one in New York. And they were there was always Mom something, and we all would eat there, and we'd run a tap like eating there, and I remember well that dinner was 50 cents then.

We weren't making a lot of money, then either, you know, but we might have three starches on a meal, you know. Anyway, you wasn't hungry. That was the main thing, you know. And then they had some ladies used to fry chicken, make sweet potato pies and come backstage and sell them, you know, and have a basket and come back there, and guys would buy things from them, you know.

So you -- all the conveniences were there, you know, and usually there was a bar somewhere around, because at the back of the -- 126th Street and Seventh Avenue, that was the Braddock Bar. All The performers hung out in there between sets, you know. The whole show almost would be around there drinking between sets, and there are other performers who'd come through town -- in town on work, and they would meet them there. You know, you'd meet all your friends there.

And you had a busy week. You know, there was something to do all the time, and it never was boring, you know. And every city that we played like that, for instance, the cities who did have those theaters at that time, as I recall, was New York -- Philadelphia had a theater; Baltimore had one, and Washington had one.

And they used to call that 'around the world.' You're going around the world circuit. So if you got those four weeks, you were doing pretty good, you know, back then. Of course, you played for choruses of chorus girls, and you'd have comedians, and you'd have dancers, tap dancers on almost all of those shows.
